packs.description: `_clip` guards against NaN but not ±inf. packs.description: In `play`, the revert for each planned change is appended to `undo` only after `await self.rpc.call(*change)` returns successfully. Snapcast JSON-RPC calls can time out (`control_timeout`) or lose the response after the server has already applied the change, for example switching a group's stream, unmuting a client, or raising volume. In that case the call raises before `undo.append(revert)` runs. The `finally` block then restores only the earlier changes, so this change stays on the snapserver permanently. The house audio is left on the announcement stream or at announcement volume. Every revert sets a setting back to its original value, so applying one for a change that never took effect is harmless.
packs.recommendation: Record the revert before issuing the change (`undo.append(revert)` followed by `await self.rpc.call(*change)`). A failed or ambiguous change then still gets reverted in the `finally` block.

Category C includes Cf (format) characters such as soft hyphen U+00AD, zero-width space/joiner U+200B/U+200D, the BOM U+FEFF and bidi marks. These normally appear inside words or emoji sequences. packs.snippet:
1| """The one config file: every other file scout reads, every service URL, and the schedule.
    2| 
    3| ``scout.yaml`` is validated by :class:`ScoutConfig` (pydantic v2, unknown keys rejected at every level).
    4| Relative paths in it resolve against the config file's own directory, so a config directory can be moved
    5| or mounted anywhere.
    6| 
    7| **Secrets never live in the YAML.** The file names an environment variable (``token_env: SCOUT_API_TOKEN``)
    8| and :func:`resolve_secret` reads it from the process environment. :func:`load_config` first loads a
    9| ``.env`` file beside the config into the environment, without overriding variables that are already set,
   10| so a real environment always wins over the file. Resolved values come back as :class:`~pydantic.SecretStr`
   11| and the config model itself holds only variable *names*, so neither its repr nor its dumps can leak one.
   12| 
   13| **Strict here, forgiving there.** The two kinds of config fail differently, on purpose:
   14|

   18| - The files it names (heartbeat policy, standing approvals, tariff, signal rules) are reloaded while scout
   19|   runs, and a bad edit to one of those degrades to defaults (or skips the bad rule) and is reported, so a
   20|   typo can't stop status updates. See :mod:`argus_scout.heartbeat`, :mod:`argus_scout.approvals` and

packs.description: Quotes are only stripped when the whole remaining value starts and ends with the same quote character. Take a line like `TOKEN="abc" # prod token`. The last character is `n`, not a quote, so the quote-stripping branch is skipped. The else branch then removes the ` #...` comment and leaves `"abc"`, with the quote characters still in the value. For a token, password or URL, this silently produces a wrong config value. The result is failed auth or failed connections, and the cause is not obvious. Common dotenv implementations support `KEY="value" # comment`.
packs.recommendation: Strip the inline comment before checking for quotes, but only outside quotes. For example: if the value starts with a quote, find the matching closing quote. Take the text between the quotes and ignore anything after the closing quote if it is whitespace or a `#` comment. Otherwise, apply the ` #` split.

packs.description: `registry.collect()` returns `prometheus_client.metrics_core.Metric` objects. These have only `name`, `documentation`, `type`, `unit` and `samples`. `_labelnames` is an attribute of the collector objects (`Counter`, `Gauge`, ...), not of the collected `Metric` families. So `getattr(family, "_labelnames", ())` always returns `()` and `declared` is always empty. The comment says this catches label names "even for a family with no samples", but it does not. A labelled metric that declares a target label (e.g. `instance` or `job`) and has not been observed yet produces no samples. It therefore passes both the registry loop and the `/metrics` text loop. The test gives false assurance about the contract it claims to enforce.

For example, iterate `registry._collector_to_names` keys, or keep references to the metric objects on the runtime, and read `collector._labelnames`. Alternatively, call `.labels(...)` on every labelled family before collecting so samples exist. Assert that the declared-label set is non-empty for at least one family, so the check cannot silently degrade to a no-op.
